reviews.title: Stop Forcing Me to Use My Primary Phone
reviews.text:
I’ve used Signal since 2020, and for years I’ve used Signal essentially only on my linked iPad. This worked perfectly fine for years.
Then, in mid-2026, Signal started forcing me to use my primary phone to keep my account active, with the warning that my account could be deleted after 120 days if the primary device doesn’t connect.
The problem is that Signal isn’t even installed on my primary phone anymore. I deliberately keep it off my phone and use Signal on my iPad for specific contacts.
So complying with this new requirement isn’t simply “open Signal on your phone.” I have to reinstall Signal, re-register/authenticate the account, which removes my existing iPad access, and then go back and relink my iPad.
In other words:
Signal works perfectly on my iPad → Signal forces me back to my primary phone → reinstall and re-register → iPad gets unlinked → relink iPad → repeat again later.
I never had to do this from 2020 through early 2026.
I am not asking for my iPad to become the primary device. I understand that the phone remains the primary device. I’m asking Signal to stop forcing me to use that device when I am actively using Signal on a linked device.
If I choose to use Signal exclusively on my iPad, that should be allowed without a recurring reinstall/re-registration/relink cycle and the threat of account deactivation.
Please stop forcing users to use their primary phone when they are actively using Signal on a linked device. This is a major regression from how Signal wor

reviews.title: Very disappointed by the complete inexistent costumer support and unclear instructions on security
reviews.text: I have now being using Signal for over 5 years and abandoned WhatsApp completely (I cannot stand Meta group) with no regrets whatsoever. The app is great, safe and has a very functional chat, everything I was looking for that WhatsApp was not giving me (such as being added to big groups with unknown numbers without my consent and ads appearing on my Facebook account based on things I had been chatting about on WhatsApp). However, I am extremely disappointed to have to report that Signal stopped working suddenly one day and the app prompted me to restore it without clearly warning me that it would completely wipe out all my chat history when reopening it. I was also never clearly notified to save the Recovery Key chain which I cannot access now as it was in the app back up before I restored it (I am a very organised person and would have copied it somewhere safe if I understood the extent of the need of it). Therefore I am now locked out of my previous account and security texts to my own mobile number are not enough to recover it without this key which I find excessive given this is not an app dealing with state secrets but only personal conversations. To add to it, no one is coming back to my emails from the support team, really disappointing considering I have been donating to the app in the past to keep it independent and going. reviews.title: Massive amounts of background activity when not in use and without permissions-what is it doing?
reviews.text: Even with the app fully closed, all permissions of any kind denied, background app refresh disabled, and without any connection to iCloud (I do not back up to any cloud), and even with cellular data use denied (WiFi only), this app conducts massive amounts of background activity and hogs the battery on my new iPhone 17 pro max (pretty hard to do). No other messaging, video, or any app does this on my phone, not even others that have end to end encryption features. There is no excuse for any app to be working so much in the background without any permission to do so, even on days it isn’t used. Hard to believe they aren’t collecting data, especially as this issue has been discussed for years with no clear answer about why it’s overriding your settings and what it’s actually doing.

reviews.title: May lose access to account when switching phone numbers
reviews.text:
Signal still requires registering with a phone number, which can be used to identify you.  SimpleX Chat requires zero identifying information. No registration and no user IDs of any kind. Don’t get me wrong, I like Signal as it’s faster and more reliable. I just wish Signal would get rid of the phone number requirement.

Let’s say you want to switch phone numbers (replace current phone number that was used to register with Signal with a new phone number).  Most carriers when you switch numbers will allow you to get a new number but you immediately lose access to your old number when the new number is activated. Unfortunately, Signal requires access to both your old and new phone numbers to be able to register the new number with your current Signal account. Signal should only require the new number if one is already logged into the app under their old number. Better yet, Signal should dump the phone number requirement altogether, or at least not rely on it as an account identifier after initial registration. They make it very difficult when switching phone numbers and when switching devices.
